title: Searching and Representing a Missing Result

blocks.text: A search needs a negative answer too

Searching for a value can end with a match or no match at all. The program must represent both outcomes. To ask only whether a value exists, initialize bool encontrado = false; and set it to true when a visited value matches. If there is no match, false retains a valid meaning; we do not need to access an invented position.
encontrado records whether any previous visit matched. A later visit that does not match must not reset it to false and erase a match that already occurred.

blocks.text: If we need the first position

To know where the target appeared, we preserve an index. We initialize posicion = datos.size() as a not-found marker: this number is not a valid index. A traversal starting at zero replaces that marker upon finding the first match and can then stop. We use posicion for access only after confirming it is less than size().

The second part of the condition keeps visits going only while no match has been found. Starting at zero and stopping on a match ensures that the stored index is the first one. The marker equal to the size is never used as a subscript.
